seasonMovement: Impossible arrival -> settlement -> navigation -> participation -> belonging -> usefulness -> chosen household -> self-defined belonging under judgment -> optional aftermath only if dramatically needed.
seasonDramaticShift: Issues 1–5 are driven largely by collision with 2026 and the work of building an ordinary life. From Issue 6 forward, modern systems remain real pressure but stop being the default dramatic protagonist. The later season is driven by what these particular people want from work, one another, New York, autonomy, responsibility, and belonging.

kinContinuity.composition: Two men and Astrid, the only woman.
kinContinuity.issues1To3: The three Kin are seen primarily together in or immediately around the Bushwick placement; they are not yet followed independently around the city.
kinContinuity.middleSeason: Their independent errands, relationships, routines and interests begin to appear individually.
kinContinuity.issues6To7: Astrid is deliberately largely absent from foreground action while the two male Kin remain visible. Her absence is ordinary, not mysterious.
kinContinuity.issue8: The courtroom reveals that Astrid has quietly become the household's most practically integrated member.
kinContinuity.maleNames: Unresolved. Do not silently lock Eirik or Ivar.

issues.title: War Council
issues.function: A Status Reconciliation Review forces the household to decide what it actually wants to defend. The question leaves the kitchen table and follows separate lives through the neighborhood before the household chooses a shared position that does not require identical futures.

issues.title: Permanent Residency / Trial by Combat
issues.function: The courtroom/hearing tests whether an institution can make a fair decision about a real but unconventional household made of separate people. Bjorn's trial is allowing others to speak for themselves; Astrid's payoff is the revelation that the least-followed member has quietly become the most practically integrated.

finaleState.ordeal: Issue 8 residency hearing functions as Bjorn's trial by combat without literal combat.
finaleState.hearingPurpose: The institution encounters a household that cannot honestly be reduced to one spokesperson, one integration narrative, or one permanent future.
finaleState.bjorn: Bjorn arrives in armor without weapons. His growth is visible when he answers for himself and protects other people's right to speak and choose instead of speaking over them.
finaleState.carrie: Carrie does not ask him to remove the armor. Her strongest testimony acknowledges that successful integration means she increasingly does not know every detail of the household's life.
finaleState.astrid: Astrid's ordinary independent competence becomes visible in court and reveals that the background member Carrie and Bjorn tracked least is the household's most practically integrated person.
